sourceDependency.note: PR137 remains the canonical authored-source ingestion lane. This blueprint is intentionally on a separate clean-main architecture branch and does not overwrite that source.

programmeShape.day1SourceException: Existing authored source currently specifies 60 minutes; rebuild should resolve this against the 45-minute standard rather than silently truncating content.
programmeShape.day3LabBoundary: Day 3 includes one 45-minute learning-to-Lab bridge plus a separate facilitated Phase A experience. The existing authored source specifies a 90-minute Part B; preserve that separation.
programmeShape.realWorldWindow: Seven-day investigation as defined by the authored Time source/runtime contract.

reportDesign.prePostRule: Compare only same-family learning/competency tasks or authored measures. A control feeling shift is self-report context, not proof of skill gain.
reportDesign.competencyNarrativeRule: For each mapped competency: state the highest evidence-supported progression level, cite the evidence class/anchor, state the limitation, then name the next evidence needed.
reportDesign.sponsorAggregateRule: Aggregate only reportable, privacy-safe competency/task evidence. Never expose personal time patterns or private reflections.

days.title: Seeing Time
days.knowledgeOutcome: Time use can be investigated through records; the story 'I have no time' is different from evidence of where time and attention went.
days.capabilityOutcome: Identify one personally relevant time moment and distinguish remembered time from a recordable event.

evidence.job: one bounded context for later investigation
check distinction between claim and record

minutes.detail: What does 'not enough time' usually mean in ordinary life?
Contrast a busy-feeling story with a simple recorded day.
Introduce record, allocation and time moment; do not yet reveal the full Time Pause.
Classify examples as story, observation or unknown.
Learner reconstructs one recent time moment.
Choose the one moment that is safe and useful to investigate.
State what is known, what is guessed and what to notice tomorrow.

days.facilitatorMove: Use the contrast between felt busyness and a record to create curiosity; do not moralise screen use or productivity.
days.carryForward: Bring one observed time moment or short record into Day 2.

days.title: Thinking Like an Investigator
days.knowledgeOutcome: Memory, observation and interpretation answer different questions; evidence becomes stronger when recorded close to the event.
days.capabilityOutcome: Convert judgements about time into reviewable observations and state what remains unknown.

evidence.job: learner states what a record can and cannot show

minutes.detail: Return to yesterday's time moment.
Compare two accounts of the same event: judgement vs record.
Observation, interpretation, evidence proximity and uncertainty.
Classify four statements.
Rewrite personal judgements as observable statements.
Create one clean observation and one open question.
Explain why the observation is stronger than the original story.

days.facilitatorMove: Keep asking 'What did you actually observe?' and 'What are you adding to the record?'
days.carryForward: Carry a clean observation and open question into the Day 3 Lab bridge.

days.title: Prepare the Time Investigation
days.knowledgeOutcome: A behavioural investigation needs a bounded situation, a prediction, a safe response to test and a clear record; the method is not the same as the explanation.
days.capabilityOutcome: Prepare a personal investigation question, prediction and smallest safe test without being told what the evidence is supposed to prove.

minutes.detail: Observation and open question.
Show why an unbounded promise such as 'manage time better' cannot be tested.
Teach investigation mechanics: situation, prediction, smallest response, evidence window. Do not give the final causal explanation.
Draft personal test on one time moment.
Record prediction and plan before the test.
Readiness, feasibility, privacy and no-opportunity logic.
Explain the separate Lab Phase A session and return path.

days.facilitatorMove: Treat the Time Pause as an investigation protocol at this point, not as proof of why the learner's pattern occurs.
days.carryForward: Separate facilitated Lab Phase A follows this 45-minute session; it may deepen Mapping, Equation and Contract but must preserve the pre-registered prediction.

days.title: What the Time Pattern Revealed
days.knowledgeOutcome: Time patterns can involve triggers, attention pulls, start friction, environmental cues, repeated routines and small leaks; these are explanations to test, not labels.
days.capabilityOutcome: Use formal concepts to explain the learner's own mapped pattern while naming alternative explanations.

evidence.job: first formal explanation after Lab discovery
distinguish trigger, leak, friction and condition

minutes.detail: What did the Lab make visible that the learner did not see on Day 1?
Compare two mapped time moments with different mechanisms.
Name trigger, pull, leak, start friction, smallest first step and environmental protection.
Choose the best explanation for short cases and explain why.
Annotate the learner's own map with formal concepts.
Write a working explanation plus one competing explanation.
Identify what real-world evidence would separate the explanations.

days.facilitatorMove: Make explanation feel like recognition of what the learner already encountered, not a lecture detached from the Lab.
days.carryForward: Watch the next eligible moments for evidence that supports or weakens the working explanation.

days.title: Evidence Studio
days.knowledgeOutcome: Eligible opportunity, missed response, partial response and no opportunity are different records; honest denominators matter more than a flattering rate.
days.capabilityOutcome: Record early experiment evidence accurately and diagnose evidence-quality problems without changing history.

minutes.detail: Return to prediction and first observations.
Compare honest no-opportunity data with a misleading perfect record.
Opportunity denominator, missingness, partial response and evidence integrity.
Classify sample tracker rows.
Review own rows without editing what happened.
Resolve recording ambiguity and mark unknowns.
State what early evidence can and cannot show.

days.facilitatorMove: Reward accurate recording, including failure and no opportunity; never reward 'good-looking' data.
days.carryForward: Continue the real-world test through the scheduled window.

days.title: Apply Under Real Conditions
days.knowledgeOutcome: A planned response must survive ordinary conditions; environment, capacity and first-step size can change follow-through.
days.capabilityOutcome: Use the planned response in real eligible moments and record what happened without retrospective score-making.

minutes.detail: What is the plan, exactly?
One case where the same plan works in one condition and fails in another.
Condition dependence, smallest first step and environmental support.
Which condition should change first?
Rehearse next eligible moment.
Review authentic observations already captured.
Name one condition to watch, not yet a permanent change to the contract.

days.facilitatorMove: Keep the focus on applying the pre-registered method; do not rescue the learner by rewriting the experiment every day.
days.carryForward: Collect the next observations with condition notes where relevant.

days.title: Experiment Clinic
days.knowledgeOutcome: A barrier is information about conditions, resources or design; a justified adjustment differs from moving the goalposts.
days.capabilityOutcome: Compare successful and unsuccessful opportunities, diagnose one barrier and make one traceable adjustment.

minutes.detail: Select one worked and one difficult opportunity.
Side-by-side comparison reveals condition differences.
Barrier vs failure; capacity vs avoidance; legitimate adjustment vs result-chasing.
Judge whether sample adjustments preserve the test.
Diagnose own evidence.
Record one justified adjustment with reason.
Predict what the adjustment should change.

days.facilitatorMove: Ask for evidence before accepting a diagnosis; preserve the original plan and adjustment history.
days.carryForward: Run the adjusted response through the remaining window and keep the original prediction available for final review.

days.title: Time Leverage and Protection
days.knowledgeOutcome: Managing one time moment is different from redesigning a time system; priority, batching, elimination, delegation, automation and protection can change the system but also create costs and responsibilities.
days.capabilityOutcome: Identify one leverage point in a time system, predict its ripple effect and choose an age/context-appropriate intervention.

minutes.detail: What has the experiment changed at the moment level?
Contrast trying harder with redesigning a weekly system.
Priority, batching, elimination, systematisation, automation, delegation and accountability.
Choose leverage methods appropriate to cases.
Map one weekly system and find a leverage point.
Predict a ripple and name a risk or cost.
Choose whether this is a future transfer test, not a mid-experiment rewrite.

days.facilitatorMove: Broaden capability without implying every learner can delegate, automate or remove structural obligations.
days.carryForward: Bring the completed seven-day record and leverage idea to evidence review.

days.title: Evidence Review and Transfer
days.knowledgeOutcome: A useful conclusion compares prediction with observation, explains uncertainty, preserves counter-evidence and asks whether the method travels.
days.capabilityOutcome: Review the full record, revise the original explanation and apply the method to a second time pattern without claiming universal success.

minutes.detail: Return to Day 3 prediction before seeing calculated results.
Prediction and observation can agree, partly agree or disagree.
Denominator, prediction accuracy, adherence/reclaim only where authored, uncertainty and counter-evidence.
What can each result legitimately support?
Complete evidence review and revise working explanation.
Map a second time pattern using the same investigation method.
State what transferred and what changed.

days.facilitatorMove: Do not turn a rate into a grade. Require the learner to compare the result with source evidence and limitations.
days.carryForward: Prepare one evidence-backed explanation and one next practice for Day 10 demonstration.

days.title: Demonstrate, Integrate and Hand Off
days.knowledgeOutcome: The programme closes by integrating what was learned, what was demonstrated, what remains uncertain and what the learner can transfer next.
days.capabilityOutcome: Teach back the investigation method, assemble a concise evidence portfolio, demonstrate transfer and set a next real-world action.

evidence.job: post learning demonstration comparable to defined starting task where applicable

minutes.detail: One sentence: what did Day 1 not yet explain?
Teach back the investigation method using a fresh short case.
Select evidence anchors: starting point, plan, observation, review, transfer.
Explain how the method changes in another context and one limitation.
Write evidence-backed progress narrative; no identity score.
Set next action/review date and close the Lab-to-learning loop.

days.facilitatorMove: Protect demonstration and transfer time; do not add new major theory.
days.carryForward: Portfolio and competency summaries become report-ready only after provenance/assessment checks.
